people: one person, unnamed and unrated (the header recorded no people, a shim bug of the time, and the game has no chat line from anyone); Armada bots: Pawns all game, one Lazarus (armrectr) with them at 6:00
our_side: seat 0, Cortex, realtime in the user's lobby; player claude-opus-5 at effort low (Claude Code 2.1.278); no LLM commander; hands: the pianist, Jev jev-latest = jev-1.13.0; started at E3 (4066, 2237); his start a mirror guess at D6 (3352, 4840), no truth file
summary: A 1v1 on Quicksilver against an unnamed Armada player, lost at about 6:13 to a Pawn rush that never let up. The build cadence matched Matt's up to the lab (0:36), but the lab picked three constructors (0:54, 0:59, 1:24) although the packet said 'one constructor first, then raiders'. With constructors and the commander on windmills, the energy store stayed under 500 from 1:09 to 3:28, so the first Grunt came at 2:08 and the commander had no D-gun during the raid. His Pawns reached our extractors at 2:04 against zero soldiers and had taken every extractor by 2:44 (793 metal lost for 108 in the first engagement). The Grunts that came after were spent badly: the five-Grunt group chased one Pawn east for 50 s while four Pawns ate home (2:39-3:29), and at 4:37-4:46 the group fought three Pawns at spot_8 while eight killed the lab beside a commander that kept assisting it on a full store. The record ends with no lab, no extractor, and the commander at 14% with nine Pawns within 700.

root.what: The lab chose a second constructor at 0:59 and a third at 1:24 (a coin flip), against the packet's 'one constructor first, then raiders'. The hands could not count from the words, and produce allowed corck with no cap. The energy stall, the empty field at 2:04 and the missing D-gun are all its cost.

our_mistakes.what: The opening packet left the count to prose ('one constructor first, then raiders'), with produce allowing corck and corak, and then waited 60 s while the lab made its picks. A stronger player makes one constructor and then only raiders, with the first Pawn or Grunt by about 1:12 (Matt's line). The tool had no cap, so the way to do it was produce [corak] once the first constructor had started.
our_mistakes.evidence: 0:37 produce {"all": ["corck", "corak"]}, wait max_seconds 60; next turn 1:37; ledger: first Grunt 2:08 (Matt 1:12)

our_mistakes.what: Everyone was put on windmills to answer the stall: constructors on wind whenever energy was low, and the commander too, under both packets (the wind at 1:35 came from the 0:37 packet's 'when energy is low' clause, the ones at 1:50, 2:06 and 2:14 from the 1:37 'everyone on wind'). The commander left the lab, and the constructors' drain kept energy under the D-gun's 500 through the raid. The people's line for this map was 1 or 2 constructors at most and about 20 energy per metal.
our_mistakes.evidence: 1:37 note 'Energy at 2/1152 with 3 constructors' worth of drain ... everyone on wind'; floor e0% 22.2, stall4 23, assist4 105; energy <500 1:09-3:28

our_mistakes.what: The player saw a lone Pawn near the E4 extractors with zero army, switched off the near-extractor wake and waited 60 s. The raid hit 8 s later, and the next turn came only on the first extractor lost.
our_mistakes.evidence: 1:56 wait {"enemy_near_extractor": false, "max_seconds": 60}, note 'Lone enemy scout at D4; no army yet'; 2:04 first corwin destroyed by armpw 1530; next turn 2:14

our_mistakes.what: The whole group went after one raider, though the packet said 'never send everybody after one raider', and stayed on that chase after a new packet said hold at home. That left four Pawns free at home through 3:07.

their_play: Armada bots, Pawn pressure from the first minute. A lone Pawn was seen near E4/D4 at 1:56 and killed a windmill at 2:04 and the first extractor at 2:13; a party of four was at (4008, 3006) by 2:30, and he reinforced without pause: 5 Pawns at 3:40, 8+3 at 4:40, 10 at 5:40, 12-13 in our base at 6:07, and a Lazarus with them at 6:00. He raided the extractors, constructors and windmills first, left the lab until 4:46 when he had eight on it, then went for the commander. His base was never seen (no unit of ours got within 2,400 of the guessed start), and nothing points to tier 2 or anything but Pawns. Our seen kills were about 20-24 Pawns (1,296 metal) against 2,312 of ours lost.

tools: direct reads of jev-0.jsonl.zst (version-1 pianist log: lab picks, group plays, parties) and record-0.jsonl (created/destroyed events, energy series)
lens.caveats: No truth file: the opponent's army, buildings and start are what we saw or the mirror guess, so minutes.py's 1.5x window at 4:00-5:00 compares against a floor and is not a real lead. No chat in the game and no people in the header: the opponent is unnamed, and the only person's word is the ledger's quote of the user. pro_baseline was not run (Quicksilver has no cards). hands_window printed only the commander's queued plays for this version-1 pianist log, so the lab's picks, the group plays and the parties were read straight from jev-0.jsonl.zst. minutes.py's 'his half' depends on the mirror guess D6, and the bot.log's start boxes are labelled the other way round from where we stood. The game is dated 2026-09-21 from the files (23:54-00:00 local); the backlog dates it 2026-09-22.
